title: Duffel, Daypack or Body? A Kilimanjaro Gear Checklist Sorted by Where Each Item Rides
meta_title: Kilimanjaro Gear Checklist: 30 Items for a Safe Summit
meta_description: Kilimanjaro gear checklist of 30 items sorted by duffel, daypack and body, with summit-night layers, sleeping bag ratings and kit to test in Kenya first.
excerpt: A Kilimanjaro gear checklist of 30 items, sorted by what you wear, what goes in your daypack and what porters carry, plus the summit-night layering order and the kit mistakes to avoid.
content:
A Kilimanjaro gear checklist comes down to about 30 items spread across three places: what you wear, what rides in a 25-35 litre daypack, and what porters carry in a duffel usually capped near 15 kg. It must cover summit-night cold well below -10°C, rain in the forest, strong equatorial sun and dry feet for six to eight days.

Most climbers from Nairobi pack the wrong things: cotton hoodies, one thin pair of gloves and boots bought the week before. Below is the full Kilimanjaro gear checklist sorted by where each item travels, plus the summit-night layers, common mistakes and how to test it all on Kenyan mountains first.

Quick Facts

  • Summit: Uhuru Peak, 5,895 m, the highest point in Africa.
  • Summit-night cold: roughly -7°C to -20°C, lower with wind chill.
  • Porter duffel: most operators cap it at about 15 kg; KPAP sets 20 kg as the most a porter should carry for the company.
  • Daypack: 25-35 litres, carrying 3-4 litres of water plus your warm layers.
  • Sleeping bag: rated for comfort around -10°C or colder.
  • Plastic bags: banned in Tanzania since 1 June 2019; pack in dry bags or stuff sacks.

How Cold Does Kilimanjaro Get Between the Gate and Uhuru Peak?

Kilimanjaro runs from farmland near 800 m to an arctic summit at 5,895 m, so a Kilimanjaro gear checklist has to cover five climate zones. Forest days feel like Nairobi in March; the final push starts at midnight in sub-zero wind. The figures below are approximate, and the night column decides your clothing.

ZoneAltitudeDayNight
Cultivated foothills800-1,800 m21 to 32°C15 to 27°C
Rainforest1,800-2,800 m15 to 20°C4 to 15°C
Heath and moorland2,800-4,000 m10 to 21°C-1 to 10°C
Alpine desert4,000-5,000 m-5 to 25°C-12 to 4°C
Arctic summit5,000-5,895 m-12 to -4°C-30 to -7°C

The alpine desert swings by more than 30 degrees between noon and midnight, and the rainforest takes up to 2,000 mm of rain a year, so pack quick-change layers and a shell.

The Kilimanjaro Gear Checklist, Sorted by Where Each Item Rides

Sorting the list by location stops you from leaving your summit gloves in a duffel that arrives at camp two hours after you. Here is the full Kilimanjaro gear checklist in 30 lines.

Where it ridesItems
On your body (9)Broken-in waterproof boots; wool or synthetic hiking socks; synthetic or merino base top; hiking trousers; quick-dry shirt; wide-brim or cap-style sun hat; UV-blocking sunglasses; liner gloves; trekking poles
In the daypack (11)Waterproof jacket; waterproof trousers; fleece mid layer; warm insulated gloves; beanie or balaclava; 3-4 litres of water (bottles or bladder); headlamp with spare batteries or a charged cable; sunscreen and lip balm; snacks; small first-aid kit with blister plasters; pack cover or liner
In the porter duffel (10)Sleeping bag (comfort -10°C or lower); down or synthetic insulated jacket; fleece-lined summit trousers; second base layer set for sleeping; spare socks (3-4 pairs); camp shoes; gaiters; toiletries and wet wipes; power bank; dry bags or stuff sacks to organise it all

On summit night the insulated jacket, summit trousers and warmest gloves move from the duffel onto your body.

What goes in the daypack on Kilimanjaro?

On any Kilimanjaro gear checklist, the daypack holds whatever you might need before camp, because porters walk ahead and you will not see the duffel until evening. Rain shell and trousers live here every day, with a fleece, gloves, a warm hat and all your water.

A 3-litre bladder such as our 3L hydration backpack keeps you sipping on the steep moorland stretches. Pair it with a one-litre bottle, since bladder tubes can freeze on summit night and a bottle carried upside down inside your jacket stays liquid longer.

What goes in the porter duffel?

The duffel carries camp and sleeping kit: bag, insulated jacket, summit trousers, spare clothes and toiletries. Keep it soft, with no wheels or rigid frame. Weigh this half of your Kilimanjaro gear checklist at home in Nairobi, because operators check bags at the gate.

Which Items Matter Most on Summit Night?

Summit night decides the climb, and it is where a weak Kilimanjaro gear checklist shows. You leave high camp at roughly 4,600-4,700 m around midnight and walk six to eight hours in the dark, slowly, often into wind.

Dress in this order, from the skin out:

  1. A synthetic or merino base layer top and leggings from our thermal base layer range.
  2. A fleece mid layer, plus a second thin one if you feel the cold.
  3. Fleece-lined trousers, such as those in our summit fleece-lined pants section, under waterproof over-trousers.
  4. An insulated down or synthetic jacket, then the waterproof shell on top if it is windy.
  5. A fleece-lined balaclava or beanie, with your hood over it.
  6. Liner gloves inside Thinsulate waterproof gloves or mittens.
  7. Two pairs of socks only if your boots still fit comfortably with both.

Our piece on layering for cold weather hikes explains why that stack works: thin layers trap more warm air than one thick coat and let you vent when the sun reaches Stella Point. Lay out these seven pieces together when you pack, and that section of your Kilimanjaro gear checklist is done.

How warm should your sleeping bag be?

The sleeping bag on a Kilimanjaro gear checklist should be comfortable to about -10°C, and many climbers prefer -15°C because high camps sit above 4,600 m. Read the comfort figure, not the extreme rating.

A snug mummy shape helps as much as the fill. Our -15°C mummy down sleeping bag is built for exactly these nights, and our sleeping bags guide explains the ratings. Sleep in a clean, dry base layer, never the one you hiked in.

Should You Buy, Rent or Borrow Kilimanjaro Gear?

Not everything on a Kilimanjaro gear checklist has to be bought. Own anything that touches your skin or shapes your feet: boots, socks and base layers. Bulky one-trip items such as a big down jacket can be hired through many Moshi and Arusha operators.

Rented kit turns up the night before, with no time to fix a broken zip. Quality thrifted gear changes that maths: pre-owned shells, fleeces and down from big outdoor brands cost far less than new, and you keep them for Mt Kenya and the next trip.

If you are shopping in Nairobi, our guide to buying Kilimanjaro gear in Nairobi covers what to look for on a thrifted rail. Common Mistakes on a Kilimanjaro Gear Checklist

Most Kilimanjaro kit problems come from three mistakes, each cheap to avoid in Nairobi before you leave.

New boots on day one

Boots need 30-50 km of walking before a long climb, ideally on hills. A sturdy, waterproof pair like the Quechua waterproof hiking boot, worn on two or three day hikes first, is safer than a premium pair straight from the box.

Cotton anywhere on the list

Cotton T-shirts, jeans and cotton socks hold sweat and freeze on summit night. Swap them for synthetic or wool layers and good merino wool hiking socks, which stay warm when damp and resist odour across several days.

Too little water capacity

Many climbers bring a single one-litre bottle. Altitude dries you out quickly, so every sensible Kilimanjaro gear checklist allows 3-4 litres of capacity, refilled with treated water at camp. Keep phone and headlamp batteries in an inside pocket too, since they drain fast below freezing; our headlamps guide covers battery choices for night starts.

Pro Tips for Your Kilimanjaro Gear Checklist

  • Weigh the duffel at home and aim for 2-3 kg under your operator's limit.
  • Pack each group (sleep, summit, spare clothes) in its own coloured dry bag.
  • Put summit gloves, balaclava and insulated jacket in one bag you can find in the dark.
  • Wear or carry your boots on the bus, never in checked luggage.
  • Leave supermarket plastic bags at home; Tanzania's ban covers visitors too.

How Can You Test Your Kilimanjaro Kit on Kenyan Mountains First?

Kenya has good test ground within a day of Nairobi. A hike up Elephant Hill or a night on Mt Kenya shows which layers, gloves and boots work long before you reach the Tanzanian gate.

The Elephant Hill hike in the Aberdares climbs to around 3,630 m through mud and cold mist, a fair rehearsal for Kilimanjaro's forest and moorland. For altitude, our Mt Kenya hiking guide covers the routes to Point Lenana at 4,985 m, where nights at Shipton's Camp come close to Kilimanjaro's high camps. When is the best time to use this kit?

Kilimanjaro's driest climbing months are January to early March and June to October. The long rains fall roughly March to May and the short rains around November and December, when the waterproofs and pack liner on your Kilimanjaro gear checklist work hardest.

Confirm current park fees and rules on the TANAPA website or with your licensed operator before you book. Porter welfare guidance, including the 20 kg load standard, is published by the Kilimanjaro Porters Assistance Project.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the most important item on a Kilimanjaro gear checklist?

Boots come first, because you wear them for six to eight days on mud, scree and frozen ground. Choose a waterproof, ankle-high pair that is already broken in. Close behind come a warm sleeping bag and an insulated jacket for summit night, since cold, not fitness, turns many climbers back.

Do I really need gaiters on Kilimanjaro?

Gaiters belong on a Kilimanjaro gear checklist. They keep rainforest mud out of your boots and stop volcanic scree pouring in on the descent from Uhuru Peak, and a light pair barely registers in the duffel. Our leg gaiters guide explains the types and how to fit them over hiking boots.

How heavy should my Kilimanjaro duffel be?

A Kilimanjaro duffel should weigh no more than your operator's limit, which is commonly about 15 kg. The Kilimanjaro Porters Assistance Project sets 20 kg as the most a porter should carry for the company. Weigh the bag at home, pack only one change of clothes for camp and wear your heaviest items on the bus.

Is Kilimanjaro colder than Mt Kenya?

Kilimanjaro is usually a little colder at the top than Mt Kenya's Point Lenana, because Uhuru Peak is about 900 m higher. Most Mt Kenya kit carries straight over to a Kilimanjaro gear checklist, with a slightly warmer jacket and gloves for the final push.

Final Thoughts

Thirty well-chosen items beat a stuffed duffel every time. Sort your Kilimanjaro gear checklist by where each piece rides, build the summit stack from skin to shell, and give boots and sleeping bag a cold Kenyan night first. This weekend, lay everything out, tick it against the table and fill the gaps.
